## Implementing AI and Machine Learning in Organisations

Implementing AI is not just a technical question — it is a question of **organisational readiness**.

| Prerequisite | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Data Quality and Governance** | AI systems are only as good as the data they are trained on. Messy, biased, or fragmented data → poor AI output. Must be addressed first. |
| **Integration with Existing Systems** | AI cannot be bolted on to the side and expected to have impact. It must connect seamlessly with existing business logic, databases, and user interfaces. |
| **Workforce Upskilling** | AI changes how work gets done — introduces new tools, new **roles**, and sometimes entire new ways of thinking. Employees need training and support. |
| **Ethics and Compliance (built in from the start)** | Especially under regulations like **GDPR** or **PDPA** (Singapore). Transparency, bias, and data privacy cannot be afterthoughts. |

### How to Get Started

- **Begin with low-risk, high-impact use cases** — pilot projects provide space to experiment, learn, and build trust with users and leadership
- **Keep humans in the loop**, especially early on — ensures oversight and context are always present

> If done right, AI can become a powerful ally — not just automating tasks, but **augmenting intelligence** across the organisation.

## The Future of System Development

| Trend | Description |
|---|---|
| **Predictive, self-healing systems** | Systems that detect and fix issues automatically |
| **AI assistants that co-develop code** | AI participates in writing and reviewing code alongside developers |
| **Low-code platforms** | Business users build their own apps without deep technical skills |
| **Intelligent automation** | Systems that tune themselves based on real-world use |
| **Ethics built into design** | Fairness, transparency, and privacy as first-class design requirements |
